coverageLevels.covered: the module classifies the item and describes how it is handled or recycled
coverageLevels.partial: named or classified in the module, but no own handling or recycling section

evidence.heading: 1.3 Sampah organik, d. Produk organik terurai lainnya + Catatan klasifikasi
evidence.says: kardus polos tanpa lapisan aluminium foil is listed as organic/biodegradable; sorting practice puts kertas and karton in anorganik daur ulang

evidence.heading: 4.3 Daur ulang kertas
evidence.says: recycling of paper in general; kardus is not named

evidence.heading: 1.2 Gambaran sampah di Indonesia
evidence.says: kertas dan karton 11,09% of national waste (SIPSN 2024)

Cardboard.note: Module 1.3 (p.7) calls plain paper and cardboard organic/biodegradable, and says everyday sorting puts them in the recyclable anorganik group because they are worth more recycled into new paper (also Bab 9 Q&A, p.34). Questions must use that wording; never state flatly that cardboard is anorganik.

evidence.heading: 1.4 Sampah non-organik, b. Sampah logam

evidence.heading: 2.6 Contoh sampah B3 rumah tangga
evidence.says: e-waste row: lead, mercury, cadmium, flame retardants, batteries; hand in to an e-waste collection point or take-back

evidence.heading: 2.7 Bahaya dan dampak B3
evidence.says: lithium batteries in phones and power banks: thermal runaway

evidence.heading: 4.7 Pengelolaan sampah B3 dan e-waste
evidence.says: copper, aluminium, gold, silver recovered by licensed facilities; delete personal data first

evidence.heading: 1.4 Sampah non-organik, c. Sampah kaca

evidence.heading: 4.5 Daur ulang kaca dan karet
evidence.says: sorted by colour, washed, crushed (cullet), melted, reshaped; recyclable many times without loss of quality

Paperboard.note: Module 1.3 (p.7) calls plain paper and karton organic/biodegradable, and says everyday sorting puts them in the recyclable anorganik group because they are worth more recycled into new paper (also Bab 9 Q&A, p.34).
